svg.title: A working day with a coordinating session, 10 November 2026
svg.desc: Strands of work on 10 November 2026. Positions show the order within a strand, not clock time. The coordinating session, Claude Code on Claude Fable 5.2, revised instruction files and skills in the afternoon. There it designed procedures for coordination, acceptance and review anew, although earlier documents already held them. In the evening it took over Research Coordination, and the pushes waited for the operator's answers to the bundled questions. Two project sessions ran alongside, one for the interface that shows the state of the projects and one for a teaching website. Several dozen subagents worked over the day, most on Opus 5.5 and those for reading, inventory and source checks on Sonnet 5.5. Project state: read-only agents compared the state file with project overviews, repositories and Git history, and another agent corrected the state file. Uncommitted work from earlier sessions was secured in separate commits in the vault and several repositories. Rules of the arrangement: a subagent aligned the rules with decisions taken that day, a reviewer with fresh context found rule sentences that were never decided and a contradiction with the assignment files, clear points were corrected and the rest put as yes-or-no questions, and a writing rule that went back to an earlier agent's wording was withdrawn. Explanation of the arrangement: the coordinating session drafted a short explanation, and an independent reader rated three statements as wrong, many more as claiming more than the files support, and found three separate episodes merged into one example. Static website: the hosted build had failed since the end of October, the cause was three images referenced as png and stored as PNG, which Windows ignores and the Linux build server does not, and after the fix the deployment ran through the same evening. A paper on Promptotyping received three independent readings, of its argument, its citations against the cited sources and its form against the journal's guidelines. Two workshop slide decks received speaker notes and were read back in full with the slide text unchanged.
